## Transparent spend feasibility experiment {#sec-transparent-experiment}

An isolated one-input, two-output relation retains the depth-32 tree, hidden asset, 128-bit amounts, ownership, commitments and nullifier rules. It compiles to 10,983 constraints. A pinned ProveKit Spartan/WHIR adapter generates and verifies actual native proofs, with Keccak, sumcheck blinding and the zero-knowledge witness-commitment mode. All 15 circuit cases and 16 native rejection checks per profile pass; both recipient ciphertexts are recovered. This experiment is not integrated into the pool.

The upstream default and twelve witness-commitment tuning profiles retain the upstream 128-bit Johnson-bound commitment target and 10-bit per-slot proof-of-work budget. The default encoded proof occupies 302,352 bytes, including required authentication hints. The smallest measured calldata floor comes from fold4-rate6: 183,728 bytes and 7,220,660 gas in a signed Prague transaction. With public inputs, ABI framing and recipient ciphertexts, the transport charge is 7,240,710 gas. These transactions perform no proof verification or payment state changes. Their charges already exceed the provisional 1,000,000-gas ceiling; they are not complete-payment gas measurements. The parameter search is bounded, and these results do not establish a lower bound for other encodings or proof systems.

The tested construction also fails a generic zero-knowledge check. For a two-row relation with identical constraints $x \cdot 1 = x$, the verifier recovers the unconstrained private witness $x$ from a transmitted alpha evaluation, despite the witness-hiding mode. The counterexample reproduces for every tested profile. It does not establish payment-key extraction. These cost and privacy results reject the tested candidate; A Solidity verifier, insertion integration and a matching Groth16 comparison are not implemented. No qualifying transparent replacement is claimed. Source, dependency pins, test scope and generated evidence are retained under `experiments/transparent/` and `benchmarks/transparent-spend.json`.
